Welcome to the 2024 Roll and Write Game Design Contest


We are set to begin the inaugural 2024 Roll and Write Game Design Contest! This is an exciting opportunity for game designers to showcase their creativity and skill in crafting engaging and innovative roll-and-write games. Whether you're a seasoned designer or just starting out, we invite you to join this contest and contribute to a vibrant community of game enthusiasts.

This year the contest will be hosted by Martin Melbardis, Alison Scott and Igor Zuber. If you have any questions please feel free to post them here on this thread or you can PM one of us.

SPONSORS
We are thrilled to announce that this contest has been graciously sponsored by the following well-known publishers and designers:
Rolling Rhino Games,
Postmark Games,
DicePen,
Keepers of Fun
and Radek Ignatów

Our sponsors are generously offering free roll and write games as prizes, in addition to the Geek gold awarded in each category. I would also like to thank an anonymous BGG user for the 1000 gold donated for this contest! 

What are roll and write games?
To those who don't know or want a clear definition...A roll-and-write game is a type of board game where players roll dice (or sometimes use other randomizers like cards) and then record the results on a sheet of paper or a score sheet. The dice rolls typically dictate what actions players can take, such as marking off sections of a grid, filling in numbers, or completing specific patterns. The goal is usually to optimize your choices based on the dice outcomes to score points or accomplish objectives.


How to Participate 

1. Design and Submit: Create a new roll-and-write game and submit it to the contest.
2. Explore and Play: Browse and print the submitted games in this contest, play them, and engage with other designers.
3. Feedback and Vote: Provide feedback to the designers and vote for your favorite games at the end of the contest.



Important Dates

• Earliest Availability: June 1, 2024
Any game that was publicly available online on BGG or other websites prior to the date of the 1st of June 2024 is not eligible for this contest.
• Submission Period: September 1, 2024 - October 1, 2024 (11:59 EST time)
New entries to the contest are accepted. By the deadline of October 1st 2024, entries must be playable, with components and rules available for download, even if they are not the final versions. no new entries will be allowed, but ongoing entries may continue to be developed
• Development Phase: October 2, 2024 - October 31, 2024
No new entries will be accepted during the development phase. Games must be "Component ready" by this date and all existing games entered can continue to be refined and changed (updates to rules, rulebook, artwork ect.)
• Freeze Period: November 1, 2024 – November 14, 2024
All entries are "frozen" during the period and cannot be changed/modified in anyway. Games must be "Contest ready" which means that all game files and rules cannot be modified to ensure that all voters evaluate the same version of the game. Players are encouraged to share feedback and suggestions, but no changes or fixes can be made until voting is complete.
• Voting Period November 15 2024 - November 28, 2024
A voting form will be made available at this time so that anyone with a BGG account can vote for their favorite games.


Contest Rules

Entry Requirements
1. Originality: Submit a new, original roll and write game. No expansions, rethemes, or reimplementations of existing games.
2. Theme and components: No restrictions on theme, components, mechanics, artwork, or game length. Games should be easy to build and play. Any amount of additional components are allowed including dice, cubes, cards and other components.
3. Availability: The game must not have been publicly available before June 1, 2024.
4. Exclusivity: The game must not be entered in any other contest.
5. BGG Page: The game should not have a BGG entry before the contest. Designers can create a BGG entry during the contest.
6. Publication Status: The game must not be published or in the process of being published during the contest.
7. Second Editions: Allowed if significantly different from the original.
8. Number of Entries: Each designer may submit up to two games to the contest. Keep in mind that each game submitted requires you to provide feedback for three other games in the contest.
9. WIP Thread: Create a WIP thread with the game name, description, and all credits.
10. Rules deadline: Ensure rules and components are available before the submission deadline of October 1st 2024. All games must be printable on regular A4 or American Letter Paper. Games must be available as free PNPs during the contest.
11. Digital Versions: Digital versions are allowed but must be accompanied by PNP files.
12. AI Use: AI can be used for artwork, ideas and other game elements.
13. Feedback Requirement: Provide feedback on at least three other games for each game you enter.
14. Copyright: You always retain all rights to your game. This is a friendly and creative community, and your ideas are safe here.
15. Flip & Writes: While the contest name specifies roll and write games, games with "flip and write" mechanisms are also allowed.
16. Each game requires a name and logo/image: Each game submitted requires a name and an image or logo to represent the game before the submission deadline of October 1st. This can always be changed before the freeze period.


Providing Feedback: 
For each game that you submit, you must provide mandatory feedback of at least 3 other games. Feedback includes:
Rulebook Read & Edits OR
Playtests + Feedback OR
Help with Artwork or setting up a TTS module.

Giving feedback is a crucial part of our contest. One might think that its sole purpose is to help the author improve their design, but it’s not true. Providing feedback is a skill and improving it will help you to become a better designer yourself. If you learn how to provide meaningful feedback, you’ll also get better at understanding and analyzing the one you received.
What is meaningful feedback? One might think that the value of feedback is subjective, however you can increase its value by keeping in mind a few suggestions:

Try to be as specific as possible
General comments such as “The rulebook was bad” doesn't help the designer to improve it. Provide rationale why you found it confusing, was it the graphical layout, order of the information or one specific wording that you had to re-read 10 times to understand?

Provide feedback that can lead to conclusions and affect improvements
“I loved your game!” is a great piece of feedback on the BGG rating page after the game is published. But is it helpful while you are developing it? It’s impossible to act on it.
Even if you think you don’t have anything meaningful to say, being more specific can be helpful to the designer. “I loved the theme and found the auction mechanism and variable goals brilliant!” is a much better piece of feedback. The designer knows what are the best parts of their game and have an easier time deciding what should be kept/cut if changes are needed.

Analyze your emotions
Games are meant to be fun, but fun can mean a lot of different things to different people. Why do you think the game was fun or boring? Try to analyze your emotions:
“The game was super fun!”:,
-because I had a lot of satisfaction when my engine kicked off in the middle of the game (great engine building implementation),
-even though the boss killed me in the last round with only 2HP left (game is tense, challenging and engaging)

“The game was boring…”:,
-because in the last 3 rounds I didn’t have anything to do (bad pacing, maybe game should be shorter or have more interesting decisions towards the end),
-because my friend was leading the whole party (there’s a quarterbacking problem in your coop game)


Spotlights events on games lacking feedback:
In order to help some game entries that have not gotten much feedback for whatever reason, we will be hosting spotlight events where the overlooked entries in the contest are highlighted in the main contest thread and testers who provide the most feedback in that time window will win prizes and geekgold..

AI Usage:
Using AI for any purpose is allowed. However, please note that using AI automatically disqualifies your game for the Best Original Artwork category.

Transparency:
While you are not required to disclose AI usage, lying about work produced by AI (if discovered) will result in immediate disqualification. This is akin to plagiarizing someone else’s texts, art, or mechanisms without proper credit. Please be honest if asked, and do not enter categories like Best Artist if you are not the artist.


Submitting a game to the contest and updating game status 

Create a WIP Thread in the WIP forum, include details of your game such as:

 Game Title/name
Designer/Artist/Graphic Designer Credits
 Link Back to this Contest's Thread: This Contest Thread
 Game Description: Provide a short paragraph describing your game.
 Image or Photo: Include an image or photo of your game.
 Links to PnP Files and Rules: Add links to the latest version of the PnP files and rules once they become available.
 Categories: List the categories you wish your game to be entered into.
 Updated PnP Files: Keep links to PnP files updated regularly.
 Announce Your Game: Post a brief intro and link to your WIP thread in the main contest thread (here) before the end of the submission period of September 1st to October 1st. 2024.
Component Ready Status: Ensure your game is ready by October 1, 2024 by having all PNP game files and components ready and adding to the thread title of your game’s WIP post a “Component Ready” status to show that your game is now ready to be playtested.
 Contest Ready Status: Ensure your game is complete and finalized by October 31, 2024. Add to the thread title of your game’s WIP post a “Contest Ready” status to show that your game is now ready finished and frozen for the remainder of the contest and cannot be changed in anyway.


Recommendations
• Low-Ink Version or online version: Provide a low-ink or online version of your game to make it easier for others to try it.
• Community Engagement: Participate actively by playing and providing feedback on other games. This enriches the experience for everyone involved.
• Please don't spam the contest thread: While announcing your game and any major updates on this main contest thread is encouraged, please don't spam this thread with excessive posts about your game.


Contest Categories 
List the categories you wish your game to be entered in on your game’s WIP page.

 Best Overall Game
 Best Solitaire Game
 Best Multiplayer Game
 Best Thematic Game
 Best Written Rules
 Best Original Artwork
 Best Graphic Design
 Best Innovative Mechanic
 Best Playtester
 Best Light/Minimal Build
 Best Family/Children Friendly Game
 Best Low-Ink Version



Voting and Prizes 
In addition to distributing 1,500 GeekGold among the top three entries in each category, the top three entries will also receive free games generously donated by our contest sponsors.

Anyone participating in or following the contest can boost the prize pool by tipping GeekGold to the posts of any or all categories posts in this contest thread.
Voting Period: November 15-28, 2024. Play as many games as possible and provide meaningful feedback.
Prizes:
GeekGold: A total of 1500 geek gold will be distributed proportionally among the top three entries in each category—40% for 1st place, 30% for 2nd place, and 20% for 3rd place. An additional 10% will be awarded during spotlight events to promote entries needing more feedback.

Roll-and-Write Game prizes: Free games donated by our sponsors (TBA).

Best Overall Game (300 )
Best Solitaire Game (100 )
Best Multiplayer Game (100 )
Best Thematic Game (100 )
Best Written Rules (100 )
Best Original Artwork (100 )
Best Graphic Design (100 )
Best Innovative Mechanic (100 )
Best Playtester (200 )
Best Light/Minimal Build (100 )
Best Family/Children Friendly Game (100 )
Best Low-Ink Version (100 )

How voting works
The top three games from each category will win geek gold and get free games from our sponsors. In addition when the voting results are posted we will be posting the rankings for every game that received votes (likely posting at least a top 10 for each category).

The voting will be conducted using Google Forms, where everyone can cast their votes to any number of entries.
The voting itself is based on 1-10 ratings in each category.

After the voting is done, we will do the following:
We analyze the data manually in order to eliminate votes coming from suspicious/shill accounts.
We calculate the weighted average for every entry in each category separately (base weight is 1, but the weight of a vote may be lower if e.g. you are the designer or artist behind the entry, you have not played it physically in case of "ease of build category" etc.)
We add X dummy votes to each entry to prevent single outliners from being ranked high (it's better to have multiple 8s and 9s than to have a single 10).
Finally we rank the games based on the average and remove the games that didn't get any votes. This is the final ranking.


Most importantly have fun
Join the contest, unleash your creativity, and have fun designing the best roll-and-write game possible! For any questions or more information, post them to the main contest thread or contact us privately. Happy designing!

*** Special thanks to Ben Morayta, Chris Hansen and John Kean for providing an awesome free template for contest guidelines
